items.title: A family of sets over a type that is not a set refutes the truncated axiom of choice

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma thm:no-higher-ac at source lines 779-781: there is a type X and a family Y over it, each Y(x) a set, for which the truncated choice principle (3.8.3) fails. The author's proof (source lines 782-796) manufactures the counterexample instead of quoting one, and the two facts required of X pull in opposite directions: univalence together with the characterisation of paths in Sigma types makes the loop space at the base point equivalent to the equivalences of the two-element type with itself, which is what shows X is not a set (source lines 784-785), while truncation induction on the witness that A is merely equal to the two-element type shows that every A occurring in X is a set and hence that X is a 1-type (source lines 787-788). The statement shows neither that the family has to be the path type to the base point nor that the contradiction is reached by observing that an actual section would make X a mere proposition (source lines 793-795).
